findings.reason: isUnknownOption (lines 972-989) returns true for a word like 'run' because hasAllShortFlags needs a leading '-' (line 946) and every hasFlagsMatching pattern starts with '^-+'. Line 225 therefore calls pushPositional before the halt branch at lines 397-399 is reached. Trigger: ['run','--verbose'] with both config flags set now gives verbose=true instead of leaving ['run','--verbose'] in `_`.
findings.claim: Removing the `/^-/` guard means that when `unknown-options-as-args` and `halt-at-non-option` are both on, plain positionals get pushed into `_` instead of stopping the parse, so the options after them are parsed.
findings.evidence: `isUnknownOption('foo')`: `negative` doesn't match, `hasAllShortFlags` returns false (no leading `-`), and every pattern given to `hasFlagsMatching` (`flagWithEquals`, `normalFlag`, ... all `^-+...`, and `negatedBoolean` `^--no-...`) needs a leading dash. So it returns `!false === true`, and `isUnknownOptionAsArg('foo')` is true. Line 225 then calls `pushPositional(arg)`, and the branch at lines 397-399 (`else if (configuration['halt-at-non-option']) { notFlags = args.slice(i); break }`) is never reached for that word. Trigger: `parser(['foo','--known','x'], {string:['known'], configuration:{'unknown-options-as-args':true,'halt-at-non-option':true}})`. The baseline sends `['foo','--known','x']` to notFlags/`_` unparsed. After the change, 'foo' is pushed and `--known` gets parsed as a flag. Nothing else does the old guard's job.

findings.reason: diff.patch touches only lib/yargs-parser.ts. The halt-at-non-option tests in test/yargs-parser.cjs:2980-3003 never turn on unknown-options-as-args, so the suite misses the C1/X1 regression. Lowered from medium to low because missing coverage is not a defect in itself.
findings.claim: The guard was removed without adding a test, and nothing covers `unknown-options-as-args` combined with `halt-at-non-option`.
findings.evidence: diff.patch changes only `lib/yargs-parser.ts`. No file under `test/` changes. The existing `unknown-options-as-args` tests (test/yargs-parser.cjs:3013-3299) never turn on `halt-at-non-option` alongside it, which is why the regression above gets past the suite.

findings.reason: Without the `/^-/` short-circuit, isUnknownOptionAsArg (line 968) calls isUnknownOption for every argument when the option is on. This runs hasAllShortFlags and six patterns through hasFlagsMatching. It is a performance point only, so it stays low.
findings.claim: Every non-dash positional now runs through isUnknownOption's regex and flag-table checks, which is wasted per-argument work.
findings.evidence: The removed `/^-/.test(arg)` short-circuit used to skip `isUnknownOptionAsArg` for non-dash args. Now `isUnknownOption` (lines 972-990) runs `arg.replace`, `negative`, `hasAllShortFlags` and `hasFlagsMatching` across 6 patterns for every positional.

findings.reason: test/tscc/lib/yargs-parser.ts:225 still has `/^-/.test(arg)`, while lib/yargs-parser.ts:225 does not. The CI optimize job (ci.yaml:92-93) builds that copy, but nothing in the project shows it must be kept in sync with the change, so it stays low.
findings.claim: The test/tscc copy of the parser still has the old guard and no longer matches lib/yargs-parser.ts.
findings.evidence: test/tscc/lib/yargs-parser.ts:225 reads `if (arg !== '--' && /^-/.test(arg) && isUnknownOptionAsArg(arg)) {`, while lib/yargs-parser.ts:225 reads `if (arg !== '--' && isUnknownOptionAsArg(arg)) {`. package.json has no script that regenerates it, so this may be a stale artefact rather than a required regeneration.

findings.reason: Line 224's comment reads 'any unknown option (except for end-of-options, "--")', but line 225 no longer requires a leading '-', so plain words also enter this branch. This is a documentation mismatch and stays low.
findings.claim: The comment says the branch handles 'any unknown option', but the branch now also catches non-option words.
findings.evidence: Line 224: `// any unknown option (except for end-of-options, "--")`. Line 225 no longer checks for a leading `-`, and `isUnknownOption` returns true for plain words such as 'foo'.
